pr_title: samples: subsys: logging: logger: Fix performance showcase
pr_body:
Sample tries to estimate maximum number of messages that can be
logged. It was using two system cycles and counting number of
messages logged in that window. It did not take into account the
fact that clock frequency may vary and logging speed also varies
(especially if LOG_IMMEDIATE is enabled). Presented results may
be faulty and misleading.

Fix is attempting to adjust window size to increase precision of
the measurement.

Fixes #21801 .

Signed-off-by: Krzysztof Chruscinski <krzysztof.chruscinski@nordicsemi.no>

issue_context.title: Logger sample's performance estimates are incorrect
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

The performance_showcase() function in samples/subsys/logging/logger/src/main.c does not estimate performance correctly.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. build samples/subsys/logging/logger with the following additional kconfig fragment in thingy_52_immediate.overlay:

```
CONFIG_USE_SEGGER_RTT=y

# CONFIG_SHELL_BACKEND_RTT is not set

CONFIG_LOG=y
# CONFIG_LOG_BACKEND_SHOW_COLOR is not set
CONFIG_LOG_BACKEND_RTT=y

CONFIG_LOG_IMMEDIATE=y
```

e.g.

```
$ west build -b nrf52_pca20020 -- -DOVERLAY_CONFIG=thingy_52_immediate.overlay
```

2. flash board and open RTT console (e.g. using Segger Ozone to load the file onto Thingy:52 via an nRF52 DK)
3. observe the following line:

```
Estimated logging capabilities: 16384 messages/second
```
4. This is plainly incorrect, since the output appears on the screen very slowly (until https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/21644 is merged), and in immediate mode, that means the logging call takes a very long time to appear https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/reference/kconfig/CONFIG_LOG_IMMEDIATE.html#cmdoption-arg-config-log-immediate.

**Expected behavior**
Estimate should accurately reflect performance of logging subsystem in immediate mode.

**Impact**
Sample performance is not accurate.


**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Toolchain gnuarmemb 07/2018
 - 4e135d76a3

review_comments: I find the purpose of this uncommented logic hard to understand. Would you mind moving it out to a helper function with a clear name?

Why is POSIX getting special treatment here too? Is this a bug in the POSIX subsystem? Maybe we can just skip this part of the sample on POSIX instead of making it harder to understand for real boards.
